Checked the control plane diffs and edge routing telemetry. Preliminary findings:

- At 08:37 UTC we saw ~18% of ClearHealth's traffic for the us-west-2 region being routed through our eu-central-1 POP (unexpected cross-region egress). This aligns tightly with the customer-observed start time.
- The change correlates with an automated peering update that rolled out at 08:30 UTC to optimize cost/latency for some customers. A selector rule intended for a small partner was too broad and matched an IP block used by ClearHealth.
- Consequence: higher RTT due to transatlantic legs and a small but impactful increase in in-flight requests leading to 502/504 errors under peak concurrency.

Mitigations applied (12:20 UTC):
- Reverted the peering selector rule and pinned ClearHealth traffic back to us-west-2.
- Enabled immediate local-fallback for their routes and increased KV cache TTL to reduce upstream calls.
- Brought up a temporary dedicated path for their highest-volume route (falls back to default after 72h).

Impact: metrics show p95 improving but p99 tails still elevated; error rate reduced ~70% from peak. We're continuing trace collection to validate full recovery.

I'll follow up with an RCA doc and diff of the routing rule. Attaching a small routing-map-diff.png and trace-snippet summary.

-Rishi

Katie —

First, apologies again for the disruption. We completed a full RCA and validation period. Summary:

Cause: a broadened peering selector rule deployed at 08:30 UTC on 2028-04-02 inadvertently matched an IP block used by ClearHealth, causing ~18% of their us-west-2 traffic to egress via eu-central-1 for ~42 minutes. The misroute increased RTT and caused transient queueing at our EU egress which, under ClearHealth's concurrency, produced elevated 502/504s and p95/p99 tail spikes.

What we did:
- Rolled back the selector and applied a strict whitelist-based selector model (no auto-broadening) — done 08:37 UTC.
- Added an emergency guardrail that prevents automated peering changes from applying to any account with active production SLAs without a canary group.
- Verified session drains and ensured no persistent sessions remained routed incorrectly; traffic has been stable in us-west-2 since rollback.
- Issued a compensatory credit for impacted usage during the incident window; Marissa will follow up with the exact credit amount and paperwork.
